user.title: Add Versatile Thermostat MPC Fan
user.description: Pick the Versatile Thermostat whose fan speed should be driven by the MPC. It must be an over_climate VTherm whose underlying climate exposes fan modes.

data.exploration_probe: Exploration probe (try an unmeasured weaker speed)

data_description.target_vtherm: The VTherm to attach to. Its control cycle drives this controller, and its underlying climate is the one whose fan speed gets set.
data_description.min_interval: Range: 1-60 min. Default: 10 min. Acts as both the floor and (x3) the cap on the adaptive interval derived from the learned dead time.
data_description.data_collection: Records one CSV row per control cycle in the Home Assistant config folder, alongside configuration.yaml: vtherm_mpc_fan_data_XXXXXXXX.csv (max 10 MB, auto-rotated). Useful for reproducing algorithm behaviour and identifying improvements during the beta phase.
data_description.defrost_entity: Optional: binary sensor, sensor or input_boolean that indicates when the heat pump is in defrost mode. VTherm does not report this, so it has to be supplied here. Compressor activity and outdoor temperature are read from VTherm directly and need no configuration.
data_description.exploration_probe: While the room holds inside the deadband, now and then (at most every 6 h per speed) step one speed down to a speed that has never been measured, so it gets learned. Abandoned as soon as the room drifts past the deadband by one sensor step. Default: on.
data_description.exploration_ucb: Near the setpoint, favour poorly measured speeds in the cost when their predicted trajectories are close to the best one. Default: off.
data_description.exploration_under_load: When the controller climbs outside a recovery, stop first at the lowest unmeasured speed that is predicted to make progress. Lengthens the climb by about one dead time. Default: off.

native_auto_fan.title: Versatile Thermostat's own auto-fan is enabled
native_auto_fan.description: This VTherm has its built-in auto-fan enabled (Auto fan mode: {auto_fan_mode}). Versatile Thermostat then sends its own fan command on every cycle, so this plugin will stand down and send nothing while it stays enabled. Open the VTherm's configuration and set Auto fan mode to None, then MPC control starts on the next cycle. Submit to create the entry anyway.

error.invalid_entity: This entity is not in the entity registry.
error.not_a_vtherm: This entity does not come from Versatile Thermostat.
error.fan_already_driven: Another plugin (such as Versatile Thermostat Auto Fan) is already driving this thermostat's fan. Only one controller can own a fan speed. Remove the other one first.

abort.already_configured: This Versatile Thermostat already has an MPC fan controller.

init.title: Edit Versatile Thermostat MPC Fan
init.description: The controller treats a speed's position in the ranking below as its strength: it drives the energy cost, the step-down safety guard, and the estimate used for speeds not yet learned. This defaults to the order the underlying climate reports, which is usually right — only change it if a speed is in the wrong position. Rank 1 is the weakest speed.

data_description.fixed_fan_hvac_modes: In these modes the fan is set to the fixed speed below, e.g. dry and fan_only. heat and cool are always regulated by the MPC and are not listed. The speed is applied as soon as the mode is entered; after a manual speed change, or after a restart or reload, it is (re-)applied only once the minimum interval has elapsed. Nothing is sent while a window is open, the unit is off or defrosting.
data_description.fixed_fan_speed: The speed used in the fixed-speed modes above (e.g. superhigh). Required when at least one fixed-speed mode is selected.
